craft_claim: Parallelism and anaphora encode ritual cadence and make a passage choral and memorable rather than merely emphatic; each repeated line should move the meaning forward, not restate it.

supporting_evidence.location: The Art of Biblical Poetry, chs. 1-3
supporting_evidence.note: Alter shows biblical parallelism is a systematic semantic movement - the second line intensifies, specifies, or complicates the first - giving ritual verse its forward pressure.

supporting_evidence.location: Masnavi, recurring refrains and paired images
supporting_evidence.note: Rumi's didactic-sacred verse uses refrain and paired figure to build cumulative, incantatory pressure across anecdotes.

scope: Anaphora and parallel-series operators; applies to devotional verse, liturgy, and cadenced prose.
exceptions: Over-repetition without semantic movement produces the saturation failure described in §H rather than devotion.
